title: introduce-conditional-tenant-metadata-guard-and-kms-scoped-jit-credentials
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: We need a lightweight guard that enforces that tenant scoping metadata (residency_zone, kms_preference, data_class) is present and validated early in the request pipeline for RBAC v2 decisions, and a short-lived KMS credentialing flow that binds issued ciphertext keys to the asserted tenant metadata. This PR implements a "conditional tenant metadata guard" that rejects requests missing required residency or KMS hints for tenants with enforcement policies, enriches the request context with canonicalized tenant attributes, and wires a new KMS JIT credential provider that issues ephemeral, region-scoped credentials bound to the tenant assertion for downstream encrypt/decrypt calls. Design summary: - request-side middleware (auth/middleware) performs schema validation against the tenant policy catalog and normalizes attributes into a canonical claim set used by the RBAC v2 evaluator. - RBAC v2 role_mappings are extended with a new attribute matcher: "tenant_metadata.asserted_zone == mapped_zone". - KMS JIT provider uses existing KMS adapter interface but returns time-limited credentials and an attestation token signed by platform KMS to prove locality before use. - audit pipeline receives additional entropy metadata (entropy_fence) to help detect tampering and duplicate forwarding across regions. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag rbac.v2.tenant_metadata_guard, start as monitor-only for 48h, then enforce for a small cohort of tenants, expand to full enforcement after compliance signoff. Backwards compatibility: existing tenants without explicit residency policies fall through to current behavior; the guard only enforces when tenant policy requires it. Testing and validation: unit tests for JSON schema validation, integration test exercising end-to-end KMS JIT handshake, and e2e perf run to verify median latency impact is <6ms on the auth path. Related tickets: ENG-1142 (attribute-driven RBAC bootstrap), SEC-78 (KMS credentialing requirements), SUP-9021 (customer incident prompting region pin checks). Checklist: - [x] schema validation and error codes - [x] RBAC role matcher extension - [x] KMS JIT provider plumbing - [x] audit entropy enrichment - [x] docs and example config - [x] integration and e2e tests - [x] feature-flag gating and gradual rollout notes

review_comments: Priya Shah: Thanks — high level this looks good. A few asks: (1) make failure modes explicit in the middleware (403 vs 422), (2) include a flag to strip tenant metadata from downstream logs, and (3) can the KMS attestation token be short-lived (<=5m)?

Asha Kapoor: Responded — addressed 1/3: added clear error codes and a new error enum; implemented a strip_metadata flag in the guard config and a redact hook in the logger; attestation token TTL is configurable with default 5m and enforced in provider tests.

Miguel Torres: Please add a lint rule or test verifying role_mappings.yaml accepts the new attribute matcher grammar. Also request adding one policy example that intentionally fails to ensure observability alerts trigger.
Asha Kapoor: Added policy-lint rule and a deliberately failing policy in tests that asserts the alert path; added CI step to run policy-lint against changed yaml files.
Liam O'Connor: Verified integration test; minor nit on variable naming in kms_jit_provider.go; approved after rename and one small unit test tweak.
ci_summary: CI: unit (pass), integration (pass), policy-lint (pass), e2e-perf (pass, median +5ms on auth path), security-scan (pass), deploy-preview (pass)
release_notes:
- Add tenant metadata guard to validate and canonicalize residency/KMS hints for RBAC v2.
- Introduce KMS JIT credential provider that issues ephemeral, region-scoped credentials bound to tenant assertions.
- Audit pipeline enrichment: entropy_fence metadata to improve cross-region dedupe and tamper detection.
Notes: Feature gated under rbac.v2.tenant_metadata_guard; rollout will be gradual and monitored.
